fixes.explanation: Whoa, hold on, friend. I think the word "distress" made you brace for a sad ending, like when the oven timer goes off and you just KNOW something's burnt. Not here! The writer says, “In my distress I called to the LORD, and He answered and set me free.” (Psalm 118:5). He called, the LORD answered, and he was set free. I've been stuck in a tight spot myself, so I know that's the ending you want.

Not quite, friend, but you're in good company, because this one is easy to rush past. The writer says, “This is from the LORD, and it is marvelous in our eyes.” (Psalm 118:23). So the LORD is the One behind the rejected stone becoming the cornerstone. MARVELOUS! That's the writer's word, and I love it. I think that's a good reason to stop mid-batch, wipe the flour off your hands, and just look at it for a second.
